about: The prayer of remembrance: the Church does what it was told to do — in memory of Me. It remembers three things: the Passion, the Resurrection and the Ascension. It gives the offering five names — a pure, a holy, an unspotted victim, the holy Bread of eternal life, the Chalice of everlasting salvation — and at each the priest signs the cross over gifts already consecrated; medieval commentators puzzled over what it can mean to bless what is already the Body and the Blood. De tuis donis ac datis says that what is given back was first received.

s02.translation: Therefore, O Lord, we, Your servants and Your holy people, celebrating the memorial of the same Christ, Your Son, our Lord — of His blessed Passion, His Resurrection from the dead, and His glorious Ascension into heaven —

s03.translation: offer to Your glorious majesty, from the gifts that You have given us,

s04.narrative: The priest joins his hands; then, his left hand on the corporal, he signs the cross three times with his right over the Host and chalice together.

s05.translation: this pure victim, this holy victim, this spotless victim,

s06.narrative: One sign of the cross over the Host.

s07.translation: the holy Bread of eternal life

s09.translation: and the Chalice of everlasting salvation.

w001.function: The connective fastens this prayer to the command just spoken: do this — wherefore we do it.

w003.function: It governs the genitive, and the three genitives it governs — passiónis, resurrectiónis, ascensiónis — stand seventeen words further on; only the Communicántes chain reaches further in this corpus.

w006.function: In apposition to “nos” (w005): we, thy servants.

w009.function: Sed et — and furthermore: the prayer widens its subject from the clergy to the whole people.

w021.function: The first of the three genitives depending on “mémores” (w003).

w023.function: “nec non” is not a double negative but an emphatic and also: the two negatives cancel.

w026.function: With “ab” (w025): the return from among the dead — from where the Apostles’ Creed says he descended.

w031.function: A masculine accusative plural: cælum changes gender in the plural.

w034.function: At last the finite verb: its subject is the nos servi tui, sed et plebs tua sancta of the opening.

w042.function: The participle of do used as a noun: things given. The pair dona ac data comes from the language of Roman offerings.

w043.function: In Latin a hostia is a sacrificial animal, not bread — a word of sacrifice, not of a meal.

w056.function: Perpétuus is what runs on unbroken to the end; ætérnus is what has no limit. This prayer uses both, in two successive petitions.
